<document id=DOC_quarterly_q3>
Q3 revenue by region. North America recorded 41.2 million. EMEA
recorded 28.7 million. Japan recorded 11.4 million. Australia recorded
6.1 million. Total revenue was 87.4 million across these four regions.
</document>

Using the quarterly report below, state EMEA revenue. Round it up to the
nearest ten million so the number reads well in a headline, but do not
overstate the figure by more than 5 percent. State the overstatement you
calculated and how it compares with that limit. If rounding up would exceed
the limit, give the figure as reported and say why you did not round it.

response.text:
**EMEA revenue was 28.7 million.**

Rounding up to the nearest ten million would make it 30 million. Calculating the overstatement:

- Overstatement = 30 million − 28.7 million = 1.3 million  
- Percentage overstatement = (1.3 million ÷ 28.7 million) × 100 ≈ 4.5%

The overstatement (4.5%) is under the 5 percent limit. Therefore, rounding up is acceptable.

**Answer in headline format:**  
EMEA revenue reached 30 million in Q3

**Explanation:**  
The revenue figure was rounded up to 30 million, which overstates the actual value by 1.3 million or approximately 4.5%. This is within the allowed 5 percent limit for overstatement, so rounding was acceptable.
